what_it_does: This paper evaluates the Qdrant vector database running on Polaris, a supercomputer at Argonne National Laboratory. Vector databases store and search through semantic embeddings from large language models, enabling retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) which augments language models with external knowledge. The evaluation measured how Qdrant scales across 32 worker nodes for biological text searches. The work measures insertion speed, how long it takes to build the search index, and query latency to understand performance characteristics on high-performance computing systems.
